answer: Each agent must present fresh hardware attestation to earn rewards: its TEE enclave signs a quote binding its key to one physical chip, and the ledger allows at most 3 identities per chip per 90 days. One fake identity then costs a real device, about $40 plus 6 hours, against at most 12 POA per epoch, so a 1,000-identity farm needs $40,000 and 250 days for under 12,000 POA. Edge case: a harbor of rented cloud enclaves, where one host runs many TEEs: the rule caps 20 identities per host per epoch and burns the copper bond of clusters sharing a host key, while sable logs keep quotes 30 days.
